title: Learning in Public
tagline: A small set of habits that compound, plus the system that keeps them findable.

clusters.label: Knowledge systems
clusters.summary: Where notes live and how they connect.

clusters.label: Publishing
clusters.summary: Turning private notes into something useful to others.

nodes.label: Learning loops
nodes.summary: Short cycles of attempt, feedback, and revision beat long cycles of consumption.
keyPoints: Feedback latency is the single biggest driver of learning speed.
Retrieval — writing it from memory — outperforms rereading, reliably.
A loop needs an artefact; without output there is nothing to correct.

nodes.label: Deliberate practice
nodes.summary: Work at the edge of what you can already do, on the specific part that fails.
keyPoints: Isolate the sub-skill; whole-task repetition hides the weak component.
Difficulty should be uncomfortable but survivable.
Track the failure mode, not the hours.

resources.label: Sliding window
resources.note: A pattern worth drilling until recognition is automatic

nodes.label: Reusable mental models
nodes.summary: Compress a domain into a handful of transferable structures instead of a list of facts.
keyPoints: A model earns its place by making a decision faster somewhere else.
Name the model — unnamed structure doesn't get reused.
Test it by finding the case where it breaks.

nodes.label: Digital garden
nodes.summary: Connected, revisable notes rather than a reverse-chronological archive.
keyPoints: Notes are living: a good one gets edited more often than it gets replaced.
Connections are the value — an isolated note is a bookmark.
Publishing pressure improves note quality more than any template.

nodes.label: Linking & structure
nodes.summary: Topics, connections, and weights that let a reader trace an idea instead of searching for it.
keyPoints: Link on the way in; retrofitting structure never happens.
Weight matters: not every note deserves equal prominence on a map.
Search is the fallback, structure is the product.

nodes.label: Plain-text pipeline
nodes.summary: Markdown in Git, static output, no database to babysit.
keyPoints: Front matter is a schema — treat it with the same discipline as any contract.
A build that fails on a missing field prevents silent content rot.
Portability is the reason to stay boring here.

nodes.label: Writing to think
nodes.summary: The draft is where the gaps in understanding become impossible to ignore.
keyPoints: Write the version you wish you had found six months ago.
If a paragraph can't be written plainly, the idea isn't finished.
Publish at 'useful', not at 'complete'.

nodes.label: Teaching & feedback
nodes.summary: Explaining to someone else is the cheapest available test of understanding.
keyPoints: Questions from readers point directly at the weakest section.
Teaching forces a sequence, and sequence is most of the insight.
Public commitments shorten the feedback loop.
